value.rationale: The real/complex Schur norm is an established functional-analytic invariant of sparse sign matrices, and the cubic prism is a canonical vertex-transitive graph family. The complete all-size exact law plus a six-phase second-order correction exhibits infinitely many strict reversals in a norm that has a smooth limit and an otherwise monotone-leading correction. The six-class boundary layer is generated by the two grid parities and the exact cutoff at one third, giving structural mathematical understanding of finite-size effects. This is not a preselected parameter table or generic textbook corollary; the oscillation and nonmonotonicity are not implied by continuum estimates alone.
